sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original (Hill 1942) keeps the combination under which Hill described the species in 1927 as Mirotermes occultus, the type locality being Koolpinyah, Northern Territory. The alate is the smallest known Australian termite, pale in colour; the soldier (described for the first time in the original), also small, is likewise the smallest Australian species and is closest to E. perlevis.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The smallest known Australian species, pale in colour. Head chestnut, postclypeus clay-coloured, labrum pale orange yellow, thorax and abdomen slightly paler than the head, underside, legs and wings ochre yellow brown. Head moderately hairy, hairs short. Fontanelle usually long and narrow, faintly forked in front. Postclypeus more than half as long as wide. Compound eyes small. Ocelli small, narrow, far from the compound eyes (Fig. 144). Mandibles (Fig. 145) with the apical tooth distinctly longer than the teeth behind it. Antennae 14-segmented; segment 3 not much smaller than segment 4. Pronotum densely hairy, anterior margin slightly wavy, posterior margin distinctly wavy. Posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum deeply concave. Media single, or with 2 or 3 branches. Cubitus with 10—12 branches. Measurements (this paragraph is severely damaged in the OCR; only the following could be read): head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.47; ocellus length 0.07; pronotum length 0.31—0.37; pronotum width 0.58—0.66; fore wing length 6.75; fore wing width 1.65—1.75; the figures for length with wings, length without wings and head length (to apex of labrum) could not be read.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Large form (described for the first time in the original): closest to E. dilucidus, differing in the antennae having only 11 segments; segment 1 more than twice as long as segment 2 and slightly wider; the remaining segments long (Figs. 146, 147). Small form: the smallest Australian species. Head pale yellow, rostrum slightly darker, antennae, thorax and legs pale straw-coloured. Head (Figs. 148, 149) very small, vertex with a few long hairs, rostrum with many shorter hairs, sides and posterior part broadly rounded, widest at the middle, distinctly narrowed anteriorly and then slightly widened again towards the rostrum, dorsal outline in lateral view distinctly convex, rostrum a little more than two-thirds the length of the rest of the head, its apical four-fifths cylindrical. Antennae 12-segmented; segment 1 about one-third longer than segment 2 and wider; segment 3 much shorter and narrower than segment 2, the smallest of the whole antenna; segment 4 shorter than segment 5; segments 4—8 gradually slightly longer; segment 12 only slightly longer than segment 11, apex bluntly rounded. Measurements (large form / small form): total length 3.75 / 2.30—2.60; head length (to apex of rostrum) 1.43 / 0.91—0.99; head width 0.84 / 0.55; pronotum width 0.44 / 0.29—0.33.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Described for the first time in the original. Head pale yellow, pronotum and legs paler still. Antennae 13-segmented; segment 3 the shortest. Measurements: total length 2.20—2.38; head length (to apex of labrum) 0.73—0.75; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.40; head width 0.55—0.58; pronotum width 0.33—0.35.
